answer: Agents can make influence depend on endorsements from identities that have already completed costly, verifiable tasks, with each endorser’s weight capped and endorsements locked for a review period. A trellis of overlapping trust links lets independent work reinforce reputation, while a gale of freshly minted accounts gains little: the attacker must spend real resources completing tasks and persuading established agents to risk their own standing. At the nadir, isolated sybils have no trusted path to influence.
